metaTitle: Unstamped Agreement Admissibility Stamp Act Rules
metaDescription: Are unstamped contracts valid in Bangladesh courts? Learn Stamp Act 1899 Sections 33-42, tenfold penalty rules, court impounding, and promissory note rules.

heroIntro: Under Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899, an unstamped or under-stamped agreement is not automatically void—it stays legally valid as a contract but is inadmissible in court evidence until impounded under Section 33 and cured by paying deficit stamp duty plus a statutory penalty up to ten times the shortfall.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Unstamped Agreements Under Stamp Act 1899
quickAnswer.text: Inadmissible as trial evidence until deficit duty and up to 10x penalty are deposited.
points: Governing Law: Stamp Act 1899 (Secs. 3, 17, 33, 35, 38, 40, 42 & Schedule I)
Evidentiary Rule: Inadmissible until cured—except criminal trials & promissory notes
Statutory Penalty: Missing stamp duty plus up to 10× deficiency (Section 35(a))
Criminal Carve-Out: Admissible directly in criminal cases (Section 35 Proviso (d))

sections.title: Legal Validity vs. Evidentiary Inadmissibility (Section 35)
sections.content:
A persistent misconception in civil litigation claims agreements typed on plain white paper instead of stamp paper are void ab initio; under Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899, revenue omissions create an evidentiary barrier at trial rather than erasing substantive contractual consent. Whenever a litigant tenders an unstamped loan acknowledgment, lease agreement, or business memorandum during evidence, the presiding Judge is statutorily bound to verify fiscal stamp compliance before admission.

Specifically, Section 35 forbids admitting any chargeable instrument in civil evidence unless properly stamped at the time of execution. Crucially, Proviso (a) empowers civil courts to cure standard commercial agreements mid-trial upon payment of missing stamp duty plus statutory penalty.

Keep in mind that stamp rules work independently from compulsory land registration statutes and differ clearly from oral payment recovery suits or cheque dishonour trials.

sections.title: How Courts Impound Documents & Calculate 10x Penalty
sections.content:
Section 33 of the Stamp Act 1899 obligates every Civil Judge, Arbitrator, or public officer receiving an under-stamped instrument to impound it until fiscal dues are settled. Opposing litigants cannot waive stamp defects by mutual consent because revenue provisions protect state fiscal rights.

Under Section 35 Proviso (a), ordinary agreements become fully admissible upon paying the deficit plus ten times the missing duty (or Tk. 5 if higher). However, promissory notes and bills of exchange face strict statutory exclusions:

Instrument TypeCurable Under Sec. 35(a)?Legal Rule & Consequence
Commercial Contract / MOUYes (Duty + up to 10x)Admissible after Sec. 42 certification
Unregistered Lease (>1 Yr)Stamp Curable OnlyBarred under Registration Act Sec. 49
Promissory Note / BillExcluded from 10x CureIncurable; sue on underlying debt proof
Criminal Case ExhibitExempt (Sec. 35(d))Admissible directly without penalty

Holders of unstamped promissory notes should plead underlying bank transfers or verified banking instruments while respecting limitation periods.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Process to Cure an Insufficiently Stamped Contract
sections.content:
Curing an impounded contract under Sections 33, 38, and 40 of the Stamp Act 1899 follows a clear court-to-Collector sequence before trial exhibits are marked. Addressing revenue gaps before witness cross-examination avoids protracted adjournments:

  1. Check Schedule I Stamp Slab at Execution Date: Verify exact non-judicial stamp value prescribed under Finance Act amendments to Schedule I of the Stamp Act 1899.
  2. File Impounding & Duty Payment Petition: Move an application acknowledging revenue shortfall under Section 35(a) requesting assessment of missing duty plus tenfold penalty.
  3. Deposit Treasury Challan or Collector Adjudication: Under Section 38(1), deposit court-assessed charges via Treasury Challan, or request District Collector referral under Section 40.
  4. Secure Section 42 Admissibility Certificate: Upon endorsement under Section 42, the court marks the contract as a valid exhibit—and Section 36 bars later appellate challenges once admitted.

Always cure agreements before requesting specific performance of bayna contracts or civil stay orders.

sections.title: Documents Exempted or Non-Curable Under Registration Law
sections.content:
Settling a tenfold stamp penalty resolves fiscal non-payment, yet cannot cure invalidity arising from failure to register mandatory instruments under Sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act 1908. Keep these statutory boundaries separate:

  • Immovable property transfers worth over Tk. 100 (Saf Kabla, Heba, mortgage, or multi-year leases) remain barred under Registration Act Section 49 even if properly stamped.
  • Post-2005 Bayna Nama sale contracts require registration within 30 days under Specific Relief Act Section 21A to compel sale deeds.
  • Standard commercial service agreements and MOUs only require proper agreement stamp paper to stay curable under Section 35(a).
  • Vouchers, money receipts, and criminal exhibits enjoy exemptions in magistrate trials under Section 35 Proviso (d).
  • NRB agreements signed overseas must be stamped within three months of arriving in Bangladesh under Stamp Act Section 18.

Confirm combined stamp and registry costs in our property registration fee guide.

sections.title: Protecting Contracts, Bayna Deeds, and Promissory Notes
sections.content:
Pre-suit verification of non-judicial stamp value, execution dates, and mandatory registration deadlines prevents fatal document exclusion during final witness examination. Remember too that once a trial judge admits an agreement into evidence, Section 36 of the Stamp Act 1899 prohibits appellate courts from overturning admissibility solely on insufficient-stamp grounds—making timely trial objection essential for defendants, and proactive curing indispensable for plaintiffs.

faqs.question: Is an agreement printed on plain white paper valid in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: An agreement written on plain paper is not automatically void if lawful offer, acceptance, and consideration exist. Under Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899, however, civil courts refuse to admit unstamped contracts as evidence until impounded and cured with deficit duty plus penalty.

faqs.question: How much penalty must be paid to cure an unstamped contract in court?
faqs.answer: Under Proviso (a) to Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899, ordinary agreements and contracts become admissible once the party pays the missing stamp duty plus a statutory penalty equal to ten times the deficiency (or Tk. 5 minimum where the tenfold amount is lower).

faqs.question: Can an unstamped promissory note be cured by paying a 10x penalty?
faqs.answer: No. Proviso (a) to Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899 expressly excludes promissory notes and bills of exchange from post-execution 10x penalty validation. Creditors holding unstamped notes must instead prove the loan independently through bank transfer trails or alternative debt acknowledgments.

faqs.question: Does the Stamp Act bar unstamped documents in criminal cases?
faqs.answer: No. Under Proviso (d) to Section 35 of the Stamp Act 1899, nothing bars an unstamped or under-stamped instrument from admission as evidence in criminal proceedings before Magistrate or Sessions Courts, including cheating, forgery, and criminal breach of trust prosecutions.

faqs.question: How soon must a contract signed abroad be stamped in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 18 of the Stamp Act 1899, instruments executed outside Bangladesh (excluding bills or notes) concerning property or acts inside Bangladesh may be stamped within three months after first arrival in Bangladesh, preventing subsequent court impounding and tenfold penalties.
